chunks: Humayd ibn Ziyad from Ubayd Allah ibn Ahmad from Ibn Abi Umayr from Al-Husayn ibn Ahmad Al-Minqari from Zurara from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said:
Indeed, among the provisions (livelihood) is that which dries the skin upon the bone.
ai.seo_question: What does it mean when a hadith says a livelihood dries the skin on the bone?
ai.summary: In this concise hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) uses the vivid imagery of skin drying and adhering to the bone to describe the physical and spiritual toll of meager or insufficient sustenance. This serves not only as an economic observation on the quality of livelihood but also as a spiritual warning, suggesting that the struggle for basic survival can distract the believer from higher spiritual pursuits and lead to a state of existential hardship. The narration highlights the importance of seeking *rizq* that is not merely sufficient for survival but conducive to a life of dignity and worship.

en.hubeali:
Humeyd Bin Ziyad, from Ubeydullah Bin Ahmad, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Al Husayn Bin Ahmad Al Minqary, from Zurara, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Earning from certain kinds of profession (trade) dries up the skin upon the bones (hard to earn).
en.sarwar: 56. Sahl ibn Ziyad has narrated from Ali ibn Bilal from al-Hassan ibn Bassam al-Jammal who has said the following: “I once was with Ishaq ibn ‘ Ammar al-Sayrafiy when a man came and he wanted something for a dinar but he had closed the shop and had sealed the sack. He then gave him the item for a dinar. I then said, ‘Fie on you, O Ishaq! I could have picked up for you a hundred thousand dirham from the ship.’

He said to me, ‘I had the same attitude but I heard abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, saying, “Whoever belittles a small amount of sustenance is deprived of its greater amount.” Then he (the Imam) turned to me and said, “O Ishaq, do not belittle small amounts of sustenance; otherwise, you will be deprived of its greater amount.’””
